speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of an itchy rash on his upper body and face. Additionally, he has been experiencing a numbness and tingling sensation on both palms. He has been working on his family's rice farm, also caring for livestock.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Larva Migrans with concurrent heavy metal toxicity or leprosy (Hansen's disease). The patient's history of working on a rice farm and caring for livestock, combined with a pruritic rash on the body/face and symmetric palmar paresthesia, strongly suggests parasitic infection or leprosy rather than the systemic autoimmune conditions I initially suspected. I need to confirm the nature of the rash and perform a skin examination to visualize the lesions. Can you describe the texture of the rash (e.g., serpiginous tracks, nodules) and has there been any loss of sensation or muscle weakness in your hands?
